dedupe_keys.name: singapore third national climate change study v3 climate projections

description: The Third National Climate Change Study (V3) of the Centre for Climate Research Singapore is presented as the world's first IPCC AR6-based climate projections at 8-kilometre resolution for Southeast Asia, with 2-kilometre projections for Singapore, under low, medium and high greenhouse gas emission scenarios, to help decision makers prepare for the impacts of global warming. The V3 site covers recent changes in Singapore's climate from stations with over 40 years of data (warming of 0.24 degrees Celsius per decade over the last 40 years), sea level change and projections broken into contributions from Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets, glaciers, land water storage, ocean dynamics and vertical land movement, a climate visualiser for Singapore and Southeast Asia, key findings, notes on extreme event indices, and a V3 data sharing portal to download the most detailed projection data. The CCRS page states that V3 results were unveiled on 5 January 2024 and follow the second study (V2) of 2015, whose data public agencies used for climate impact studies. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): NEA copyright (contents owned by or licensed to NEA). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the most detailed data is behind the separate data sharing portal. Coverage is Singapore and Southeast Asia. It supports climate adaptation and hazard exposure analysis of drainage, coastal defences, power and transport under future heat, rainfall and sea level; related records are the CMIP6 climate projections in the CDS and the IPCC AR6 sea level projections.
